provenance.workload_source: seeded synthetic Poisson arrivals; not calibrated to production traces

dp_laplace.mechanism_design_claim: For add/remove-one-request adjacency over this fixed horizon, the bounded discrete sampler has a conditional (epsilon, delta) guarantee for the declared count/event transcript under independent uniform random bits; it is not a code audit or an end-to-end runtime guarantee.
dp_laplace.artifact_guarantee: conditional on OS-CSPRNG output modeling independent uniform bits and the documented sampler/calibration; no independent implementation audit
dp_laplace.adjacency: workload request lists differ by exactly one added or removed Request record over the whole fixed horizon; not user-level adjacency
dp_laplace.composition: basic approximate-DP sequential composition over the fixed public release count; each per-tick integer arrival vector has L1 sensitivity at most 1
dp_laplace.postprocessing_boundary: discrete noise is added to per-tick integer arrival counts; nonnegative clipping, EWMA smoothing, scaling targets, epoch, instance counts, scale events and cold-start counts are post-processing; no true queue term and no downscale/retirement, so worker busy state cannot alter observed pool counts or launches
exclusions: same person/data spanning multiple sessions or deployments
response latency/errors, sampler execution timing/CPU, and workload-private performance outputs
external billing or other runtime transcript
dp_laplace.randomness: os_csprng: each noise sample draws fixed-size random bits from Python secrets/OS CSPRNG; the finite-rational capped-geometric sampler has a stated approximate-DP bound under the documented assumptions

methodology: Known-policy diagonal nearest-centroid profiler on current, previous and cumulative observer counts/events only. First half independent sessions profile; second half test. Session classes balanced across each half; trial-pooled balanced recall. Equal-weight independent trial bootstrap with5000 resamples. Public function pool identities are visible. Demand task is binary latent session demand regime, not exact arrival recovery. Uniform workload has no hot-function task.
limitations: Function-affine fixed-service single-request workers; no runtime/ORAM/network integration. Simulated seconds, not measured service latency. Horizon-censored requests count as SLO violations; p95/p99 concern completed requests only. Price is a hypothetical configurable input. The legacy noisy policy has no adjacency/sensitivity/composition guarantee. The optional dp_laplace sampler has a conditional event-level approximate-DP bound only for its declared fixed-horizon count/event observer with independent hidden uniform random bits; the recorded deterministic-seed experiment itself has no DP guarantee. This is not a formal code audit. No user-level or full-runtime guarantee, or universal attack bound. Public count/event observer excludes queue, true arrivals, response latency, sampler execution timing/CPU, billing, active scheduling and joint transcripts. Imported repeated traces support performance only. Pareto membership uses point estimates, not significance tests. No policy dominance required or forced.
